transitions.historical_text: When there is a monster on your opponent's side of the field after this monster's first attack of your Battle Phase, this monster can attack once again during the same Battle Phase. In addition, negate the effect of a Trap Card that targets this card and destroy it. If this card is Special Summoned from the Graveyard by another card's effect, you must Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster on your side of the field.
transitions.summary: Era condition on the second attack: the GOAT script adds `not e:GetHandler():IsDirectAttacked()` to the extra-attack condition, so Tyrant Dragon only attacks again if its first attack was made against a monster; the modern script grants the second attack whenever the opponent controls a monster afterwards, including when the first attack was direct. Upstream annotates it 'Only gains the extra attack if battled a monster'. No English printing states the restriction - every version says only 'after this card's first attack' - so this is a period ruling, and its chronology is unresolved.

transitions.summary: Wording only, on period rulings (round 037, 2026-09-29). The record claimed: Era text 'If this card is Special Summoned from the Graveyard by a card effect, you must Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster' (the revival succeeds and the Tribute is owed afterwards) versus the 2013 text 'cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard, unless you Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster' (no revival without a Dragon to Tribute). A period ruling in force says otherwise: Konami TCG Skilled White Magician Card FAQ (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If you activate "Monster Reborn" to Special Summon your opponent's "Tyrant Dragon" in your opponent's Graveyard, you must still Tribute a Dragon-Type monster from your side of the field. If you do not control a Dragon-Type monster, you cannot select "Tyrant Dragon" as a target for "Monster Reborn"." No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

review.notes:
Implementation gap flagged, not invented: upstream itself annotates this variant 'not fully implemented', and the script diff contains no difference in the Graveyard-revival effect, so the GOAT variant enforces the modern post-2013 'cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard unless you Tribute' restriction rather than the pre-errata 'Tribute owed after the Summon' behaviour that the 2005 and 2010 snapshots require. Reproducing that would need a custom script; the baseline is still the best available and is kept as reuse-upstream. Two further script-diff hunks are API-equivalent and not recorded: `aux.DoubleSnareValidity(c,LOCATION_MZONE)` versus the hand-rolled effect registering code 3682106 ('Double Snare'), and `re:IsTrapEffect()` versus `re:IsActiveType(TYPE_TRAP)`. Trailing cosmetic v5 -> v6 (SS02-ENA07, 2019-01-24: 'target this card on the field', 'GY', 'Dragon monster') is not recorded as a change. The extra-attack ruling and the 2013 erratum cannot be sequenced against each other because the former has no chronology at all.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Tyrant Dragon). A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: Era text 'If this card is Special Summoned from the Graveyard by a card effect, you must Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster' (the revival succeeds and the Tribute is owed afterwards) versus the 2013 text 'cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard, unless you Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster' (no revival without a Dragon to Tribute). Contradicted by Konami TCG Skilled White Magician Card FAQ (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If you activate "Monster Reborn" to Special Summon your opponent's "Tyrant Dragon" in your opponent's Graveyard, you must still Tribute a Dragon-Type monster from your side of the field. If you do not control a Dragon-Type monster, you cannot select "Tyrant Dragon" as a target for "Monster Reborn"." Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "This is because Tributing a Dragon-Type monster is a condition on the Summoning of the card; it is not part of the effect." The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. Verdicts: [c2] d1 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: 'If this card is Special Summoned from the Graveyard by a card effect, you must Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster' became 'This card cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard, unless you Tribute 1 Dragon-Type monster'. Under the historical text the revival succeeds and the Tribute is owed after the fact; under the errata'd text the revival is simply illegal without a Dragon available to Tribute. The same printing reworded the Trap negation as 'Negate any Trap effects that target this card, and if you do, destroy that Trap', which the script diff shows is not a behavioural change."
